Equations: Human: dS_h/dt = Λ_h − λ_h S_h − μ_h S_h; dE_h/dt = λ_h S_h − (k_h + μ_h)E_h; dI_h/dt = k_h E_h − (γ_h + μ_h)I_h; dR_h/dt = γ_h I_h − μ_h R_h. Mosquito: dS_m/dt = Λ_m − λ_m S_m − μ_m S_m; dE_m/dt = λ_m S_m − (k_m + μ_m)E_m; dI_m/dt = k_m E_m − μ_m I_m, with λ_h = β_h I_m/N_m and λ_m = β_m I_h/N_h in the 2025 formulation. [1]
Assumptions: Closed or demographically balanced populations; one exposed and one infectious class in each species; no vertical transmission, no loss of human immunity, and no mosquito recovery in the 2025 model. The 2022 variant adds panic/stress/anxiety-related human removal terms. [1] [3]
Forecasting Strength: Best-established as a mechanistic baseline and useful for equilibrium, R0, sensitivity, and scenario analysis; the cited papers primarily emphasize mathematical analysis and simulation rather than prospective operational forecasting. [3] [4]
Main Limitation: Fixed transmission and incubation/recovery parameters, homogeneous mixing, and coarse compartments can miss weather-driven seasonality, changing mosquito abundance, importation, serotypes, and reporting variation. Forecasting reviews emphasize that these assumptions constrain predictive ability. [5]

[6]
Assumptions: Same seven-compartment host–vector structure as the deterministic model, but β_h and γ_h vary with virus load v; mosquito recruitment is A, and mosquitoes do not recover. [6]
Forecasting Strength: Scientifically useful for representing parameter uncertainty and heterogeneity, but not the strongest evidence base for operational forecasting: the paper focuses on fuzzy stability, R0, and simulations rather than validated prospective outbreak forecasts. [6]
Main Limitation: The virus-load membership functions introduce flexibility but require assumptions or data for the virus-load distribution; they do not by themselves solve time-varying weather, mosquito-density, spatial, or reporting processes. [6]

The structural form is the baseline seven-compartment system above, augmented by an ensemble Kalman filter that updates hidden states and parameters as observations arrive. [7]
Assumptions: Mechanistic transmission model plus sequential assimilation of reported dengue observations; practical performance depends on observation model, ensemble initialization, parameter updating, and the assumed relationship between reported cases and latent infections. [7]
Forecasting Strength: The strongest direct forecasting candidate among the strict SEIR–SEI papers found: it was validated in synthetic experiments, applied to historical cases in three cities, and reported better predictions than comparator SEIR- and SIR-EnKF models. [7]
Main Limitation: The retrieved source record does not provide enough equation and validation detail to assess the exact transmission terms, observation model, or calibration choices; the paper should be consulted before implementation. [7]

Model Family: Weather- and mosquito-informed data-assimilated vector model (SIR/EAKF comparator, not strict SEIR–SEI)
Representative Papers: Chen et al. (2022), An ensemble forecast system for tracking dynamics of dengue outbreaks and its validation in China. [8]
Equations: Uses an SIR-type human–mosquito model rather than a strict SEIR–SEI system, with mosquito birth μ_b(t), mosquito death μ_d, temperature-linked transmission τ(t), horizontal transmission, vertical transmission through dissemination U, and an effective population size updated during assimilation. [8]
Assumptions: Constant human population with no human birth/death; time-varying mosquito population from seasonal birth and constant death; perfectly mixed populations; vertical transmission; seeded infected mosquitoes; clinic reports represent 35% of weekly new infections in the model. [8]
Forecasting Strength: Although not strict SEIR–SEI, it is the strongest forecasting benchmark in the retrieved evidence: retrospective Guangzhou forecasts across seven seasons achieved >85.7% peak-time accuracy one week ahead, >71.4% peak-intensity accuracy one week ahead, and 57.1% total-incidence accuracy one week ahead; the system also outperformed GAM and SARIMA in the reported comparisons. [8]
Main Limitation: It omits exposed compartments and therefore does not represent human or mosquito latent periods explicitly; its performance depends on local mosquito surveillance, temperature relationships, effective-population updating, and the reporting assumption. [8]
